findings.title: Missing Access Control in updateTreasuryFee
findings.invariant: Only owner should be able to update treasury fee percentage
findings.attack: 1. Deploy malicious contract calling updateTreasuryFee with high fee (e.g., 50%). 2. All swap fees would go to attacker's address. 3. Drain all trading fees from pool.
findings.impact: Complete theft of all accumulated trading fees, financial loss for liquidity providers

findings.title: Reentrancy in removeLiquidity
findings.invariant: State updates should occur before external calls
findings.attack: 1. Create malicious token contract. 2. Call removeLiquidity which sends tokens before updating balances. 3. Malicious token callback reenters removeLiquidity. 4. Withdraw more than entitled share.
findings.impact: Draining of pool reserves, theft of LP funds

findings.title: Uninitialized Protocol Fee
findings.invariant: Protocol fee recipient should be initialized at deployment
findings.attack: 1. Deploy pair contract without setting feeTo. 2. Protocol fees accumulate but cannot be withdrawn. 3. Permanent loss of protocol revenue.
findings.impact: Loss of protocol revenue, inefficiency in fee distribution
